searchText: need more eyes on https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/583, anyone using `kzg_commitments` from the event? (note we will keep emitting them until gloas either way but drop them for slots after gloas) I like it, as before, it's artificial now to have those involved, the CL has to fetch them separately IMO the gloas version is just a separate event you mean without bumping the event version? the current way the events are defined (bascially using the example data as schema) isn't great, so it's hard to express pre/post fork types, but we kinda did the same with the attestation event too and it didn't cause issues also considering they are just JSON so adding/removing fields across forks shouldn't be a huge deal well, in which case the version should be bumped the overriding principle for me is that these messages are raw-ish transcriptions there is no version on the events though this one is not anymore so give it a different name informal versioning they should not rely on the client to look up anything from a database etc the fulu version did not but glosa changes how columns work we discussed this for eletrca regarding the attestation event and the outcome was that we are fine with changing the format instead of adding a attestation_v2 event that works too let me find the discussion around this, seems to be the same problem we have now that's what I suggested back then https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/461, devs didn't like it ok, I don't deeply have preferences as to how to do this but "It might be expensive to get them from the bid." which is enough for me for them to be gone from the SSE I'm fine with 583, I'm fine with other approaches too from implementer side is seems to be the preference to remove kzg commitments, also align more with spec type mostly asking consumers here if they use them for something but post gloas it's different anyways <@&1416139337179074590> ^^ xatu very likely uses that event, but I don't think any other tool from our side does. do you use `kzg_commitments`? or better question, even if you do, would you still want them after gloas ^ <@84562395988508672> my intiuition is that anyone who uses these events it purely interested in timing information, not the actual data of the event yeah, it's mostly timing data we use it to determine blob count but we can derive that elsewhere, definitely not a blocker 🙂 tyvm for checking

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: need more eyes on https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/583, anyone using `kzg_commitments` from the event? (note we will keep emitting them until gloas either way but drop them for slots after gloas)

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: I like it, as before, it's artificial now to have those involved, the CL has to fetch them separately

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: IMO the gloas version is just a separate event

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: you mean without bumping the event version? the current way the events are defined (bascially using the example data as schema) isn't great, so it's hard to express pre/post fork types, but we kinda did the same with the attestation event too and it didn't cause issues also considering they are just JSON so adding/removing fields across forks shouldn't be a huge deal

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: well, in which case the version should be bumped

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: the overriding principle for me is that these messages are raw-ish transcriptions

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: there is no version on the events though

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: this one is not anymore

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: so give it a different name

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: informal versioning

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: they should not rely on the client to look up anything from a database etc

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: the fulu version did not but glosa changes how columns work

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: we discussed this for eletrca regarding the attestation event and the outcome was that we are fine with changing the format instead of adding a attestation_v2 event

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: that works too

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: let me find the discussion around this, seems to be the same problem we have now

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: that's what I suggested back then https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/461, devs didn't like it

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: ok, I don't deeply have preferences as to how to do this but "It might be expensive to get them from the bid." which is enough for me for them to be gone from the SSE

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: I'm fine with 583, I'm fine with other approaches too

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: from implementer side is seems to be the preference to remove kzg commitments, also align more with spec type

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: mostly asking consumers here if they use them for something but post gloas it's different anyways

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content: xatu very likely uses that event,  but I don't think any other tool from our side does.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: do you use `kzg_commitments`?

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: or better question, even if you do, would you still want them after gloas

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: my intiuition is that anyone who uses these events it purely interested in timing information, not the actual data of the event

excerpts.author: samcm
excerpts.content: yeah, it's mostly timing data

excerpts.author: samcm
excerpts.content: we use it to determine blob count but we can derive that elsewhere, definitely not a blocker 🙂

excerpts.author: samcm
excerpts.content: tyvm for checking
